record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Functional Analysis and Function Theory
record.original_question: Let X be a Banach space, let X be a subspace of a Banach space X1, and let f: X -> R be a z-linear functional, meaning that there is a constant C such that for every finite family x1, ..., xn in X one has |sum_i f(x_i) - f(sum_i x_i)| <= C sum_i ||x_i||. Writing Z(f) for the infimum of such constants, does every such f admit an extension F: X1 -> R with the same z-linearity constant Z(F) = Z(f), or at least what structural reason explains whether such preservation should hold?

evidence.quote: The extension result follows now taking a bounded projection m : X1 → X and then a linear projection L : X1 → X and setting F = bm + `L. This is a z-linear map F : X y R that extends f. The problem of such rude way of extension is that Z(F) can be much larger than Z(f).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space which is a closed subspace of a Banach space $X_1$. A map $f: X \to \mathbb{R}$ is called z-linear (or quasi-linear) if it is homogeneous and there exists a constant $C \geq 0$ such that for every finite family $x_1, \dots, x_n \in X$,
$$\Big| \sum_{i=1}^n f(x_i) - f\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\Big) \Big| \leq C \sum_{i=1}^n \|x_i\|.$$
Let $Z(f)$ denote the infimum of all constants $C$ for which the above inequality holds.

Question: Does every z-linear functional $f : X \to \mathbb{R}$ admit an extension to a z-linear functional $F : X_1 \to \mathbb{R}$ (i.e. $F|_X = f$) satisfying $Z(F) = Z(f)$? More generally, identify the structural reason that determines whether such an isometric-type preservation of the z-linearity constant under extension can be achieved (as opposed to extensions where $Z(F)$ is strictly larger than $Z(f)$).
artifact.status_search_result: Web search on z-linear (quasi-linear) maps and the Kalton–Peck theory shows the relevant nonlinear Hahn–Banach-type framework, with results bounding distances from z-linear maps to linear ones by $Z(F)$. However, no source directly resolves whether every z-linear functional on a subspace extends to the larger space with the same constant $Z(F) = Z(f)$. The status of this specific isometric extension question appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.claim: Defines z-linear maps and the constant Z(F), framing the extension problem but not resolving isometric preservation.

status_evidence.title: Kalton and Quasi-Banach Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Extensions of Banach spaces are represented by quasi-linear maps via Kalton–Peck theory.
status_evidence.claim: Provides general framework for quasi-linear extensions but does not establish Z(F)=Z(f) preservation.

status_evidence.title: The behaviour of quasi-linear maps on C(K)-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies extension and behaviour of quasi-linear maps with constants.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on quasi-linear map extension behaviour without directly answering the equality of constants question.
